title: 22. Interview: How to prepare for system design interviews
summary: Interview Q&A for How to prepare for system design interviews.
objectives: Answer the How to prepare for system design interviews interview questions out loud
Lead with the concept, then a small example, then a tradeoff

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body: A step-by-step guide on **how to prepare** for system design interviews at top tech companies.

sections.title: Understanding the Interview Format
sections.body:
### What Companies Look For:

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ EVALUATION CRITERIA                                    │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ 1. Problem Understanding (20%)                         │
│    • Do you ask the right questions?                   │
│    • Can you identify requirements?                    │
│                                                        │
│ 2. System Design Skills (30%)                         │
│    • Can you design scalable systems?                  │
│    • Do you know when to use what?                     │
│                                                        │
│ 3. Technical Knowledge (25%)                           │
│    • Database, caching, load balancing                 │
│    • Understanding of trade-offs                       │
│                                                        │
│ 4. Communication (15%)                                 │
│    • Can you explain your thinking?                    │
│    • Do you listen to feedback?                        │
│                                                        │
│ 5. Problem Solving (10%)                              │
│    • Can you identify bottlenecks?                     │
│    • Do you optimize effectively?                      │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Typical Interview Structure:

**Duration:** 45-60 minutes

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Phase 1: Introduction (2-3 min)                 │
│  • Brief intro                                  │
│  • Interviewer explains the problem             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                    ↓
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Phase 2: Requirements Gathering (5-7 min)       │
│  • Ask clarifying questions                     │
│  • Define functional requirements               │
│  • Define non-functional requirements           │
│  • Agree on scope                               │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                    ↓
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Phase 3: High-Level Design (15-20 min)         │
│  • Draw architecture diagram                    │
│  • Explain major components                     │
│  • Discuss data flow                            │
│  • Identify APIs                                │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                    ↓
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Phase 4: Deep Dive (15-20 min)                 │
│  • Database schema                              │
│  • Scaling strategies                           │
│  • Handle specific scenarios                    │
│  • Discuss trade-offs                           │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                    ↓
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Phase 5: Q&A (3-5 min)                         │
│  • Your questions                               │
│  • Interviewer feedback                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

sections.title: Preparation Timeline
Study Strategy
sections.body:
### Phase 1: Build Foundation (Week 1)

**Day 1-2: Core Concepts**
```
Morning:
  □ Read: Scalability, Availability, Reliability
  □ Learn: Vertical vs Horizontal Scaling
  □ Understand: Latency vs Throughput
  
Afternoon:
  □ Practice: Calculate QPS for different scenarios
  □ Draw: Simple 3-tier architecture
  
Evening:
  □ Watch: YouTube videos on scaling
  □ Read: Engineering blogs (High Scalability)
```

**Day 3-4: Caching & Load Balancing**
```
Morning:
  □ Study: Cache eviction policies
  □ Learn: Load balancing algorithms
  □ Run: Python cache examples
  
Afternoon:
  □ Practice: Design caching strategy for Twitter
  □ Implement: Simple LRU cache in Python
  
Evening:
  □ Review: When to use caching
  □ Quiz yourself: Cache trade-offs
```

**Day 5-7: Databases**
```
Morning:
  □ Study: SQL vs NoSQL comparison
  □ Learn: Sharding, Replication
  □ Understand: ACID vs BASE
  
Afternoon:
  □ Practice: Design database schema for e-commerce
  □ Draw: Master-slave replication diagram
  
Evening:
  □ Read: Database case studies (Netflix, Uber)
  □ Review: Database selection criteria
```

### Phase 2: Learn Components (Week 2)

**Component Checklist:**

```python
components_to_master = {
    'Load Balancer': {
        'know': [
            'Round robin, Least connections, IP hash',
            'Layer 4 vs Layer 7',
            'Health checks'
        ],
        'can_explain': 'When to use each algorithm',
        'practice': 'Design load balancing for 1M users'
    },
    
    'Cache': {
        'know': [
            'LRU, LFU, TTL',
            'Cache-aside, Write-through, Write-behind',
            'Cache invalidation strategies'
        ],
        'can_explain': 'Trade-offs of each pattern',
        'practice': 'Design caching for read-heavy system'
    },
    
    'Database': {
        'know': [
            'When to use SQL vs NoSQL',
            'Sharding strategies',
            'Replication (master-slave, master-master)'
        ],
        'can_explain': 'Database selection criteria',
        'practice': 'Design database for Instagram'
    },
    
    'Message Queue': {
        'know': [
            'Pub-sub pattern',
            'Queue vs Topic',
            'At-least-once vs exactly-once delivery'
        ],
        'can_explain': 'When to use async processing',
        'practice': 'Design notification system'
    },
    
    'CDN': {
        'know': [
            'How CDN works',
            'Cache headers',
            'Origin servers'
        ],
        'can_explain': 'When to use CDN',
        'practice': 'Design video streaming with CDN'
    }
}
```

### Phase 3: Practice Systems (Week 3)

**Must-Practice Systems:**

#### 1. URL Shortener (Easy - 45 min)
```
Practice Focus:
  □ Requirements gathering
  □ Hash function design
  □ Database schema
  □ Scale to 1B URLs
  
Key Learning:
  • Hash collisions
  • Base62 encoding
  • Database indexing
  • Cache strategy
```

#### 2. Twitter (Medium - 60 min)
```
Practice Focus:
  □ Fan-out on write vs read
  □ Timeline generation
  □ Follower/following system
  □ Scale to 500M users
  
Key Learning:
  • Hot celebrity problem
  • Push vs pull model
  • Cache invalidation
  • Database partitioning
```

#### 3. Instagram (Medium - 60 min)
```
Practice Focus:
  □ Photo upload & storage
  □ News feed generation
  □ CDN strategy
  □ Scale to 1B photos/day
  
Key Learning:
  • Object storage (S3)
  • Image processing pipeline
  • Feed ranking algorithm
  • Sharding strategy
```

#### 4. Uber (Hard - 60 min)
```
Practice Focus:
  □ Real-time location tracking
  □ Matching algorithm
  □ WebSocket/SSE for updates
  □ Geographic data structures
  
Key Learning:
  • QuadTree/Geohashing
  • Real-time systems
  • Pub-sub for notifications
  • Surge pricing
```

#### 5. YouTube (Hard - 60 min)
```
Practice Focus:
  □ Video upload & transcoding
  □ Video streaming
  □ CDN distribution
  □ Scale to 1B views/day
  
Key Learning:
  • Video encoding pipeline
  • Adaptive bitrate streaming
  • CDN strategy
  • Recommendation system basics
```

sections.title: Practice Methodology
sections.body:
### Daily Practice Routine:

```python
class DailyPractice:
    """How to practice effectively"""
    
    def design_system(self, system_name, time_limit=45):
        """
        Practice designing a system
        
        Steps:
        1. Set timer (45-60 minutes)
        2. Design on paper/whiteboard
        3. Don't look at solutions
        4. Review after completion
        """
        
        steps = {
            'step_1': {
                'time': '5 min',
                'task': 'Requirements',
                'questions': [
                    'What are functional requirements?',
                    'What scale are we targeting?',
                    'What are constraints?'
                ]
            },
            'step_2': {
                'time': '5 min',
                'task': 'Estimation',
                'calculate': [
                    'QPS (avg and peak)',
                    'Storage requirements',
                    'Bandwidth needs'
                ]
            },
            'step_3': {
                'time': '15 min',
                'task': 'High-Level Design',
                'draw': [
                    'Architecture diagram',
                    'Data flow',
                    'Major components'
                ]
            },
            'step_4': {
                'time': '15 min',
                'task': 'Deep Dive',
                'detail': [
                    'Database schema',
                    'API design',
                    'Scaling strategy',
                    'Bottlenecks'
                ]
            },
            'step_5': {
                'time': '5 min',
                'task': 'Review',
                'check': [
                    'Did I meet requirements?',
                    'Can it scale?',
                    'What trade-offs did I make?'
                ]
            }
        }
        
        return steps
    
    def self_review_checklist(self):
        """Questions to ask yourself after each practice"""
        return [
            '✓ Did I ask clarifying questions?',
            '✓ Did I do capacity estimation?',
            '✓ Is my diagram clear and well-organized?',
            '✓ Did I identify bottlenecks?',
            '✓ Did I discuss trade-offs?',
            '✓ Can my design handle the scale?',
            '✓ Did I consider failure scenarios?',
            '✓ Would I be able to implement this?'
        ]
```

sections.title: Mock Interview Practice
sections.body:
### How to Conduct Mock Interviews:

**Option 1: With a Friend**
```
Setup:
  1. Find a study partner (in-person or online)
  2. Take turns being interviewer/interviewee
  3. Use real interview questions
  4. Set 45-minute timer
  5. Give honest feedback

Benefits:
  ✅ Practice communication
  ✅ Get real-time feedback
  ✅ Identify weak areas
  ✅ Build confidence
```

**Option 2: Self-Practice**
```
Setup:
  1. Record yourself (video or audio)
  2. Design system on whiteboard
  3. Explain out loud as if interviewer is present
  4. Review recording
  5. Note areas for improvement

Benefits:
  ✅ Practice anytime
  ✅ See your body language
  ✅ Check speaking pace
  ✅ Identify filler words
```

**Option 3: Online Platforms**
```
Platforms:
  • Pramp (free peer interviews)
  • interviewing.io (paid, with engineers)
  • Exponent (paid, with prep courses)
  • LeetCode (system design problems)

Benefits:
  ✅ Interview with strangers (realistic)
  ✅ Get professional feedback
  ✅ Practice under pressure
  ✅ Access to many problems
```

### Mock Interview Schedule (Week 4):

```
Monday:     Design URL Shortener (Easy warmup)
Tuesday:    Design Twitter (Medium difficulty)
Wednesday:  Design Instagram (Medium difficulty)
Thursday:   Design Uber (Hard difficulty)
Friday:     Design YouTube (Hard difficulty)
Saturday:   Random system (interviewer picks)
Sunday:     Review all weak areas
```

sections.title: Common Mistakes to Avoid
sections.body:
### 1. Jumping to Solution Too Quickly
```
❌ WRONG:
Interviewer: "Design Twitter"
You: "We'll use Cassandra, Redis, and..."

✅ RIGHT:
Interviewer: "Design Twitter"
You: "Let me clarify requirements first.
     Should we focus on posting tweets and timeline?
     How many daily active users are we targeting?
     What's the expected QPS?"
```

### 2. Not Doing Calculations
```
❌ WRONG:
"We'll need a database and some caching..."

✅ RIGHT:
"With 100M DAU, 10 actions/day:
 QPS = 100M × 10 / 86400 ≈ 11,574
 Peak QPS ≈ 23,000
 So we need multiple database replicas..."
```

### 3. Over-Engineering
```
❌ WRONG:
"We'll use Kubernetes, Kafka, Elasticsearch,
 microservices, service mesh, ML models..."

✅ RIGHT:
"Let's start simple with load balancer,
 application servers, and database.
 Then we can add caching and scale horizontally..."
```

### 4. Not Asking Questions
```
❌ WRONG:
Silently designing for 30 minutes

✅ RIGHT:
"Should we support video uploads?
 What's the priority: consistency or availability?
 Do we need real-time updates?"
```

### 5. Poor Communication
```
❌ WRONG:
Designing silently, then presenting final solution

✅ RIGHT:
"I'm thinking of using a cache here because...
 The trade-off is...
 Does this make sense?
 Should I continue or do you have questions?"
```

### 6. Ignoring Trade-offs
```
❌ WRONG:
"We'll use NoSQL because it scales better"

✅ RIGHT:
"NoSQL gives us better horizontal scalability,
 but we lose ACID transactions and complex queries.
 For this use case, eventual consistency is OK,
 so NoSQL is a good choice."
```

sections.title: Week Before Interview
sections.body:
### Daily Checklist:

**7 Days Before:**
```
□ Review all fundamental concepts
□ Practice 1 system design (with timer)
□ Review your weak areas
□ Read: Company engineering blog
```

**6 Days Before:**
```
□ Mock interview (record yourself)
□ Review: Common system designs
□ Study: Company's tech stack
□ Practice: Drawing diagrams quickly
```

**5 Days Before:**
```
□ Practice 2 different systems
□ Review: Capacity estimation formulas
□ Study: Trade-offs of different approaches
□ Rest well (don't over-study)
```

**4 Days Before:**
```
□ Mock interview with friend/platform
□ Review feedback from mock interview
□ Practice: Asking clarifying questions
□ Create personal cheat sheet
```

**3 Days Before:**
```
□ Light practice (don't burnout)
□ Review: Quick reference guide
□ Practice: Speaking clearly and confidently
□ Prepare questions to ask interviewer
```

**2 Days Before:**
```
□ One final mock interview
□ Review all notes
□ Watch: System design interview videos
□ Relax and exercise
```

**1 Day Before:**
```
□ Light review only (no new topics)
□ Review: Your cheat sheet
□ Prepare materials (pen, paper, water)
□ Get good sleep (8+ hours)
```

sections.title: Day of Interview
sections.body:
### Morning Routine:

```python
class InterviewDay:
    """Your interview day routine"""
    
    def morning_prep(self):
        """What to do before interview"""
        return {
            '2_hours_before': [
                'Eat a good breakfast',
                'Quick review of cheat sheet (10 min)',
                'Practice one simple system (URL shortener)',
                'Do NOT learn new concepts'
            ],
            '1_hour_before': [
                'Set up your space (quiet, good lighting)',
                'Test your video/audio',
                'Have pen and paper ready',
                'Keep water nearby'
            ],
            '30_min_before': [
                'Take deep breaths',
                'Do light stretching',
                'Review common phrases to use',
                'Be confident!'
            ]
        }
    
    def during_interview(self):
        """Tips during the interview"""
        return {
            'first_5_min': [
                'Listen carefully to problem',
                'Take notes',
                'Ask for clarification if needed',
                'Smile and be friendly'
            ],
            'requirements_phase': [
                'Ask about functional requirements',
                'Ask about scale (users, QPS)',
                'Ask about priorities',
                'Confirm scope with interviewer'
            ],
            'design_phase': [
                'Think out loud',
                'Start simple',
                'Draw clear diagrams',
                'Check with interviewer regularly'
            ],
            'deep_dive_phase': [
                'Listen to interviewer hints',
                'Discuss trade-offs',
                'Show you know multiple approaches',
                'Be open to feedback'
            ]
        }
    
    def key_phrases_to_use(self):
        """Helpful phrases during interview"""
        return {
            'starting': [
                '"Let me make sure I understand the requirements..."',
                '"To clarify, are we focusing on..."',
                '"What scale are we targeting?"'
            ],
            'designing': [
                '"I\'m thinking of using X because..."',
                '"The trade-off here is..."',
                '"Does this make sense so far?"'
            ],
            'when_stuck': [
                '"Let me think through this for a moment..."',
                '"Could you give me a hint on..."',
                '"What aspect would you like me to focus on?"'
            ],
            'discussing_tradeoffs': [
                '"Option A gives us X but costs Y..."',
                '"We could also use Z, which would..."',
                '"Given our requirements, I think..."'
            ]
        }
```

### Interview Checklist:

**Before You Start:**
```
□ Pen and paper ready
□ Water nearby
□ Quiet environment
□ Good internet connection
□ Confident mindset
```

**During Requirements:**
```
□ Ask about users and scale
□ Ask about read/write ratio
□ Ask about latency requirements
□ Ask about consistency needs
□ Confirm scope
```

**During Design:**
```
□ Start with high-level diagram
□ Explain each component
□ Discuss data flow
□ Think out loud
□ Check for feedback
```

**During Deep Dive:**
```
□ Show database schema
□ Discuss scaling strategies
□ Identify bottlenecks
□ Propose solutions
□ Discuss trade-offs
```

**At End:**
```
□ Summarize your design
□ Ask about edge cases
□ Ask for feedback
□ Ask your questions
□ Thank the interviewer
```

sections.title: Progress Tracking
Final Tips for Success
sections.body:
### Mental Preparation:

```
✅ Confidence:
   "I've studied 30+ hours. I'm prepared."
   
✅ Positive Mindset:
   "This is a conversation, not an interrogation."
   
✅ Accept Imperfection:
   "There's no perfect solution. Trade-offs are OK."
   
✅ Stay Calm:
   "Take a breath. Think before speaking."
```

### Technical Preparation:

```
✅ Know Your Formulas:
   • QPS = Daily Requests / 86,400
   • Storage = Items × Size × Replication
   • Bandwidth = QPS × Avg Response Size
   
✅ Know Your Components:
   • When to use cache
   • When to use message queue
   • SQL vs NoSQL criteria
   
✅ Know Common Patterns:
   • Master-slave replication
   • Sharding strategies
   • Cache eviction policies
```

### Communication Tips:

```
✅ Speak Clearly:
   • Don't rush
   • Use simple language
   • Pause to think
   
✅ Engage Interviewer:
   • Ask if they follow
   • Listen to hints
   • Be open to suggestions
   
✅ Show Your Process:
   • Think out loud
   • Explain reasoning
   • Discuss alternatives
```

sections.title: You're Ready!
sections.body:
Remember:
- **System design is about trade-offs, not perfect solutions**
- **Communication is as important as technical knowledge**
- **It's OK to not know everything - show your thinking process**
- **Practice makes perfect - the more you practice, the better you get**

**Good luck with your interview! You've got this! 💪**
